strengths: The restrained contrast and saturation treatment improves material separation without replacing the source lighting design.
Warm plaster remains tonally differentiated while the cool rainy scene preserves its blue-orange practical-light relationship.
Thresholded bloom retains bright fixture shapes and does not create broad halos or erase highlight structure.
The corrected colour-channel treatment avoids the blue central island and shadow banding visible in the rejected colorbalance iteration.
The finish transfers across square warm-material and vertical dark-atmospheric sources without changing delivery topology.
limitations: This is a display-referred medium-distance finishing profile, not a substitute for physically authored lighting, exposure, material response, depth grading, or shot-specific colour direction.
The deliberately subtle bloom, vignette, and grain may be nearly invisible after aggressive social-platform recompression and should not be intensified globally to compensate.
Hero close-ups and HDR mastering require separate profiles and dedicated skin-tone and highlight evidence.
notes: Accepted on the third visual iteration. Iteration one crushed dark coverage and introduced a green-biased cast. Iteration two exposed that FFmpeg colorbalance on the selected planar path created severe shadow hue segmentation. The final implementation uses luminance-preserving color-channel gains and a reduced vignette while retaining fail-closed black/highlight gates.
